config.hero: a night-shift pharmacist who notices everything and says nothing
config.setting: an all-night drugstore on Sunset Boulevard

bible.title: The Midnight Dose
bible.premise: Behind the marble counter of the Palms Drugstore, you measure cough syrup and keep your mouth shut for Hollywood's night owls. When a dead producer's lethal prescription box is slipped into your drop-slot, three smiling regulars return with guns in their pockets.
bible.heart: Your promise to keep your mute delivery boy safe from the vultures who run Sunset Boulevard.
bible.goal: Expose the schemer who planted the poisoned tonic in your dispensary and clear your counter before trouble lands.
bible.danger: A trio of desperate regulars will swear any lie, flip any bargain, or crack any skull to walk out with the fatal bottle.
bible.world: The Palms Drugstore on Sunset Boulevard smells of peppermint and cold zinc, lit by buzzing red neon. The front counter houses a marble soda fountain, while the locked dispensary safe sits in the cramped back room. Across the asphalt sits the velvet-draped Mocambo Club, and the back alley runs behind studio soundstages.

characters.name: Wanda
characters.description: A torch singer from the Mocambo whose polished smile hides an envelope full of blackmail photos.

characters.name: Nolan
characters.description: A heavy-jawed beat officer who takes free nickel sodas and sells precinct secrets to the highest bidder.

characters.name: Lester
characters.description: A jittery studio assistant who sweats through his collar and clutches a torn receipt that is not his.

characters.name: Boyd
characters.description: A slick-haired loan shark in a tailored gabardine coat who never raises his voice and never forgets a debt.

rules: The dispensary safe requires a four-number combination known only to you.
The glass telephone booth by the front door is tapped by the Mocambo club.
Nobody walks behind the prescription counter without an invitation or a drawn piece.
Every medicine bottle has a handwritten batch number on the bottom label.

pages.text:
Night shifts at the Palms Drugstore usually cost you only coffee and quiet. You watch the front door from behind the counter and protect Pip. Pip cannot speak, but he sweeps the tiles and sleeps safely in your back room. You promised his mother the boulevard would not swallow him.

The brass mail slot clatters. Pip scampers over and brings you a parcel wrapped in twine. Inside rests an amber bottle marked for Marcus Vance, the studio boss who died three hours ago. The prescription label bears a lethal dose of digitalis and tonight's date.

Heavy boots halt outside. Officer Nolan rattles the locked glass, tapping the pane with his nightstick.

choices.text: Stash the poisoned bottle before letting Nolan inside.
Open the door immediately and confront Nolan on the sidewalk.

factsAdded.text: You hold a bottle of lethal digitalis addressed to the late Marcus Vance.
Pip is safe inside the drugstore with you.
Officer Nolan is demanding entry at the front door.

pages.illustrationPrompt: a glass-paned drugstore door under the dark night sky

pages.choiceText: Stash the poisoned bottle before letting Nolan inside.
pages.text:
You shove the amber bottle beneath the soda fountain drainboard, hidden behind the mint syrup. You wave Pip into the dark storeroom, then turn the lock to let Nolan inside.

Officer Nolan steps in, heavy boots scuffing the black-and-white tile. His nightstick swings like a pendulum. "Saw a shadow at your mail slot," he rumbles, leaning over the counter. "Marcus Vance didn't die of old age tonight. The precinct traced a fatal dose of digitalis to your register."

His thumb hooks into his gun belt. "Hand over the bottle, pal. Keep quiet, and the mute kid stays out of juvenile court."

choices.text: Pour Nolan a soda and play dumb about the delivery.
Demand to see an official precinct warrant.

factsAdded.text: The lethal digitalis bottle is hidden under the soda fountain drainboard.
Officer Nolan threatened to frame Pip for Vance's poisoning.
Pip is hiding in the back storeroom.

pages.illustrationPrompt: an amber glass medicine bottle tucked behind jars under a counter

pages.choiceText: Open the door immediately and confront Nolan on the sidewalk.
pages.text:
You slide the glass vial deep into your coat pocket, twist the deadbolt, and step beneath the yellow buzz of the streetlamp. Officer Nolan leans against the brick, twirling his nightstick. His heavy jaw sets into a smile that never touches his eyes.

"Evening, Doc," Nolan rumbles, blocking your doorway. "Dispatch got a funny tip. Said Marcus Vance had a special bottle delivered here tonight. The kind that puts folks to sleep for good." He lowers his voice. "Hand it over, and I forget this shop was ever named."

Behind the glass, Pip watches with wide, frightened eyes. Nolan wants the poison, but he might just be clearing tracks for the real killer.

choices.text: Deny having the bottle and threaten to call the precinct.
Invite Nolan inside for a soda to discover who tipped him.

factsAdded.text: Nolan knows a lethal bottle for Vance was delivered here.
You kept the poison hidden in your pocket.

pages.illustrationPrompt: a streetlamp casting a pool of yellow light on the sidewalk

pages.choiceText: Deny having the bottle and threaten to call the precinct.
Invite Nolan inside for a soda to discover who tipped him.
Pour Nolan a soda and play dumb about the delivery.
pages.text:
You draw a heavy fountain glass, squirt in dark cherry syrup, and blast it with fizzy water. Sliding it across the marble, you offer your best easy grin. Nolan does not touch the soda; his thick hand rests heavy on his service revolver.

"Cut the comedy," Nolan growls. "A studio chief is dead, and someone is taking the fall." Before he can reach for the counter gate, the front door chimes. In scurries Lester, Vance’s jumpy studio assistant, clutching a torn receipt in trembling fingers.

Lester freezes, his collar soaked through with sweat. "I need Mr. Vance's package," he squeaks, looking between you and the law. "He swore it arrived here tonight."

choices.text: Tell Nolan that Lester's receipt looks stolen.
Offer to search the locked dispensary safe for Lester.

factsAdded.text: Lester arrived clutching a torn receipt and demanding Vance's package.

pages.illustrationPrompt: a heavy service revolver resting in a leather holster on a police belt

pages.choiceText: Demand to see an official precinct warrant.
pages.text:
Nolan rests a heavy hand on his holstered revolver and scoffs. "A warrant? Warrants take judges, pal. Judges take time Marcus Vance’s friends don't want to waste."

That tells you plenty: Nolan is freelancing off the clock for an easy payoff. Before the cop can barge behind the counter, the front door rattles. A young man with a soaked collar presses against the glass, clutching a torn receipt. It is Lester, Vance’s jumpy studio assistant.

Nolan’s heavy jaw tightens. He glares at the glass, stepping back into the shadows by the display rack. "Keep that latch thrown," the cop mutters. "Lester is trouble."

choices.text: Unlock the front door and let Lester inside.
Keep the door locked and confront Nolan about his buyer.

factsAdded.text: Nolan is hunting the digitalis without a precinct warrant.
Lester is rattling the locked door clutching a torn receipt.

pages.illustrationPrompt: A heavy service revolver resting in a worn leather holster.

pages.choiceText: Tell Nolan that Lester's receipt looks stolen.
pages.text:
You raise a hand and point at Lester’s fluttering grip. "That receipt was torn right out of Vance’s private ledger, Officer. The kid swiped it." Nolan pivots toward the trembling assistant, his heavy jaw set tight.

"Is that right, ink-slinger?" Nolan barks, hauling Lester up by his damp lapels.

Lester gasps, tears welling behind his round spectacles. "Wanda made me do it! The singer from the Mocambo Club! She told me to fetch Vance's digitalis or she’d publish Marcus’s diary!"

Nolan’s greedy eyes light up. A dead tycoon's diary is worth a fortune on Sunset Boulevard. He loosens his grip, distracted by the prospect of bigger blackmail.

choices.text: Slip into the back room to check on Pip.
Demand Lester explain Wanda's connection to the poison.

factsAdded.text: Lester confessed that Wanda, the Mocambo singer, sent him for the digitalis.
Lester revealed that Wanda holds Marcus Vance's secret diary.

pages.illustrationPrompt: a raised hand pointing an accusing finger across a drugstore counter

pages.choiceText: Offer to search the locked dispensary safe for Lester.
pages.text:
You nod and step through the storeroom door toward the safe. Anything to buy time and check on Pip.

In the shadows, the kid crouches behind a tower of towel crates. He catches your sleeve, his small face tight with panic, and thrusts a calling card into your palm. It belongs to Boyd, the neighborhood loan shark. Scrawled on the back in purple ink are eight words: Drop the bottle, Lester. Vance is already cold.

Lester didn't come to fetch a boss's tonic. He came to clean up a hit. Out front, Nolan's nightstick raps against the wooden partition. "Hurry it up in there," the law barks. "My patience doesn't run on credit."

choices.text: Confront Lester with Boyd's note in front of Nolan.
Tell Nolan that Lester is working for the loan shark.

factsAdded.text: Found Boyd's note exposing Lester as the bottle planter.

pages.text:
You stride back to the soda fountain and slap Boyd's card onto the marble counter. "Boyd sends his regards, Lester," you say. "He says Vance is already cold, so you can stop playing errand boy."

Lester turns the color of curdled milk. His knees knock against a swivel stool. "Boyd set me up!" he squeals. "He told me it was just heartburn powder to slip into the safe! He swore Vance owed him ten grand!"

Nolan's heavy paw clamps onto Lester's shoulder like a vise. Headlights sweep across the front window, cutting through the red neon. "Boyd doesn't leave loose ends," Nolan mutters, reaching for his holster. "And he knows which cop takes his cut."

choices.text: Sneak Pip out the alley door before Boyd arrives.
Pressure Lester to name who ordered the hit at the Mocambo.

factsAdded.text: Lester confessed Boyd tricked him into planting the poison.
Officer Nolan admitted he takes payoffs from Boyd.

pages.illustrationPrompt: a small calling card with purple handwriting resting on a marble counter

pages.choiceText: Tell Nolan that Lester is working for the loan shark.
pages.text:
You step out from the back room and slap Boyd's calling card onto the marble counter. Nolan glares down at the purple ink, his thick thumb twitching over his revolver. "Lester," Nolan rumbles, "you miserable squealer."

Lester turns the color of curdled milk. He lunges across the fountain, knocking over a row of glasses with a deafening crash. "Boyd made me do it!" Lester shrieks, clawing at your apron. "Vance owed Boyd fifty grand! I only dropped the box!"

Nolan shoves Lester hard against the stools, his eyes gleaming with sudden greed. Nolan smells Boyd's racket now. He wants that poison bottle for himself, to squeeze the loan shark dry.

Offer the hidden bottle to Nolan in exchange for Pip's safety.
